turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—first, can you tell me when the yellowing of your skin/eyes started and whether it began suddenly or gradually? Doctor: Also, have you had dark urine, pale stools, fever, or severe right-upper-belly pain?
Patient: It started about a week ago and felt more gradual than sudden. I’ve noticed my urine getting darker, but I haven’t had fever or severe right-upper-belly pain. I’m not sure about pale stools.

Doctor: Any itching of the skin or unintentional weight loss, and do you drink alcohol heavily or take acetaminophen/any new meds or supplements? Doctor: Also, have you had nausea/vomiting, easy bruising/bleeding, or confusion (possible liver dysfunction)?

Patient: Yes, I’ve had some itching, but not major weight loss. I’ve been mostly using alcohol on weekends and I haven’t taken acetaminophen or any new meds that I can recall—though I did use cocaine and ecstasy occasionally. I’ve had nausea with some vomiting and I’ve also been bleeding from the nose with easy bruising, and I’ve felt confused and not oriented.

Doctor: Thank you—next, have you noticed yellowing of the gums/eyes worsening with time and any swelling of the legs/abdomen or vomiting blood/black tarry stools? Doctor: Also, any history of viral hepatitis (jaundice after travel, IV drug use), prior liver disease, or a recent illness/tick exposure?

Patient: The yellowing has been getting worse over the past week, but I don’t think I’ve noticed leg or belly swelling. I haven’t vomited blood or had black tarry stools, and I don’t have a history of viral hepatitis or prior liver disease. I did have a recent illness with no clear cause, but no tick exposure or travel that I can recall.

Doctor: Given the progressive jaundice over a week plus dark urine, itching, nausea/vomiting, nose bleeding/easy bruising, and confusion without fever or severe RUQ pain, I’m concerned about acute liver failure—likely from toxin/drug-induced hepatitis (including alcohol and occasional cocaine/MDMA). Doctor: I need urgent labs and coagulation status—REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive metabolic panel (AST/ALT, bilirubin, ALP, GGT), INR/PT, CBC, ammonia, acetaminophen level, viral hepatitis panel (A/B/C/E), and urine toxicology.

RESULTS: Temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F); Blood Pressure 110/60 mm Hg; Heart Rate 94/min; Respiratory Rate 13/min. Neurological: Not oriented to time and space; asterixis present (possible liver failure). Skin: Jaundice on skin and mucous membranes. ENT: Epistaxis noted. Blood Work: Hemoglobin 16.3 g/dL; Hematocrit 47%; Leukocyte Count 9,750/mm3; Neutrophils 58% (Bands 2%); Eosinophils 1%; Basophils 0%; Lymphocytes 24%; Monocytes 2%; Platelets 365,000/mm3. Liver/Coagulation: Bilirubin 25 mg/dL (elevated); AST 600 IU/L (elevated); ALT 650 IU/L (elevated); TP Activity < 40%

Doctor: Your labs (bilirubin 25, AST/ALT ~600–650), low total protein activity <40%, and confusion with **asterixis** strongly suggest **acute liver failure**; the next step is to confirm severity urgently with clotting. Doctor: REQUEST TEST: **INR/PT**, **serum ammonia**, and **acetaminophen level now**; simultaneously start **IV N-acetylcysteine** while results are pending and involve ICU/emergency. Doctor: Given the timing (about a week), no chronic liver history, ongoing toxin exposure risk (alcohol and occasional cocaine/ecstasy), and hepatic encephalopathy, DIAGNOSIS READY: **Acute liver failure—likely toxin/drug-induced hepatitis (e.g., alcohol/illicit drug–related), with hepatic encephalopathy and coagulopathy**
